question: When the public record says a building's facade window is open, does the building then buy the work?

sources.name: DOB NOW: Safety – Facades Compliance Filings

queries.label: facade Initial Permits, General Construction
queries.where: work_type='General Construction' and filing_reason='Initial Permit' and (work_on_floor like '%Facade%' or upper(job_description) like '%FACADE%' or upper(job_description) like '%FISP%' or upper(job_description) like '%LOCAL LAW 11%' or upper(job_description) like '%LL11%' or upper(job_description) like '%LL 11%' or upper(job_description) like '%PARAPET%' or upper(job_description) like '%EXTERIOR WALL%' or upper(job_description) like '%POINTING%' or upper(job_description) like '%LINTEL%' or upper(job_description) like '%TERRA COTTA%' or upper(job_description) like '%CORNICE%')

queries.label: sidewalk-shed permits, every filing reason and status

sources.name: DOB NOW: Build – Job Application Filings

queries.label: repair jobs behind the UNSAFE cohort's permits
queries.where: job_filing_number in (the jobs of those permits, 100 per request)

facadePermit.regex: DOB NOW Approved Permits (rbx6-tga4): work_type 'General Construction', filing_reason 'Initial Permit', same BIN, work_on_floor contains 'Facade' OR job_description contains any of FACADE, FISP, LOCAL LAW 11, LL11, LL 11, PARAPET, EXTERIOR WALL, POINTING, LINTEL, TERRA COTTA, CORNICE (case-insensitive). One job counts once (job number before the dash), dated by its earliest issued_date.
facadePermit.workOnFloor: As the regex definition, but only permits whose work_on_floor (DOB's own work-location field) contains 'Facade'.

definitions.firstReport: A building's earliest xubg-57si filing with filing_type 'Initial' and a filing_date in the cycle; its filing_status is the report's status.

headline.claim: Of 2,523 NYC buildings whose first Cycle-9 facade report was filed UNSAFE, 40.3–50.4% pulled a facade repair permit within 24 months (28.8–34.7% within 12), against 3.4–4.9% of buildings reported SAFE.
headline.window: first cycle-9 report filed 2022-02-01..2024-09-21, followed 730 days
headline.definition: regex definition; the lower bound of each range is the work_on_floor-only definition

headline.claim: Those permits came a median 231 days after the report and declared a median $227k (IQR $100k–$540k), $630.6M in all.
headline.window: first cycle-9 UNSAFE report filed 2022-02-01..2024-09-21; first permit within 730 days
headline.definition: estimated_job_costs on the permit application; a permit is a proxy for a signed contract

headline.claim: 398 different contractors won those 1,272 jobs; the ten busiest hold 18.9%.
headline.definition: distinct applicant_license on the first facade permit

headline.claim: Facade repair is not a concentrated market: 2,176 licensed GCs pulled facade permits since 2022; the top 10 hold 10.2% and the busiest 1.5% (3,114 GCs and 8.9% on the wider definition).
headline.denominator: 12,041 facade jobs with a GC permittee
headline.definition: work_on_floor definition (the wider regex definition in parentheses); one job counted once

headline.claim: Buildings with six months left and no report filed: 39.1–44.2% filed within 6 months and 62–63.9% within 12, in each of three sub-cycles; 413 engineering firms filed cycle-9 reports and the top 10 hold 20.1%.
headline.definition: first cycle-9 Initial report filed after the replay date

headline.claim: 64.5% of sidewalk sheds at FISP buildings ended with a facade repair permit; a shed standing over a year with none converted at 30.9–34.9% within 24 months, against 49.2–53.9% for a shed under a year old.
headline.definition: regex definition; sign-off is w9ak-ipjd signoff_date

headline.claim: Today 259 buildings have a cycle-10 report filed UNSAFE in the last 12 months and no facade repair permit since (nor in the six months before it): Manhattan 153, Brooklyn 52, Bronx 35, Queens 19; 0 of them are on the register.
headline.window: four register boroughs, first cycle-10 report filed UNSAFE 2025-09-22..2026-09-22
headline.definition: the FRESH_UNSAFE window: not a signal the register has yet

nonClaims.claim: The register's ranking puts the buyers on top.
nonClaims.evidence: Top 800 by the register's facade score against the rest of the flagged pool, facade permit within 24 months: 2021-08-21 24.8% vs 22.7% (+2.1 pts); 2022-08-21 20.8% vs 23.8% (-3 pts); 2023-08-21 23.5% vs 24.5% (-1 pts).
nonClaims.rule: counted as holding only if the top beats the rest by at least 3 percentage points at every replay date

nonClaims.claim: UNSAFE_PRIOR buildings (UNSAFE last cycle, nothing filed this cycle) buy more than the unflagged baseline.
nonClaims.evidence: At or below the NOT_FLAGGED baseline at 1 of 3 replay dates: 2021-08-21 14.4% vs 13.9%; 2022-08-21 12.6% vs 17.5%; 2023-08-21 26.3% vs 16.9%.
nonClaims.rule: holds only if above the baseline at every replay date

nonClaims.claim: CHRONIC_NON_FILER buildings (no report last cycle, nothing this cycle) buy more than the unflagged baseline.
nonClaims.evidence: At or below the NOT_FLAGGED baseline at 2 of 3 replay dates: 2021-08-21 16.4% vs 13.9%; 2022-08-21 16.6% vs 17.5%; 2023-08-21 12.1% vs 16.9%.
nonClaims.rule: holds only if above the baseline at every replay date

nonClaims.claim: A long-standing shed with no repair permit (SHED_NO_REPAIR) is the best facade lead.
nonClaims.evidence: 2023-09-21: 30.9% within 24 months vs 49.2% for a shed under a year old; 2024-03-21: 34.9% within 24 months vs 53.9% for a shed under a year old. It reads as a stuck owner, not a ready buyer.
nonClaims.rule: holds only if it converts at least as well as a new shed at every replay date

nonClaims.claim: A facade permit is a signed contract, and its declared cost is the contract value.
nonClaims.evidence: A permit is the public trace of a hired contractor; the cost is the applicant's own estimate on the permit application.

nonClaims.claim: Venue openings (SLA licences, DOHMH) or City Record award timing are backtested here.
nonClaims.evidence: This script measures facades and sheds only. A pending liquor application has no key to the licence it becomes, so its lag can only be logged going forward; make no timing claim for venues or awards from this file.

caveats: A permit is a proxy for a purchase: it shows a licensed contractor was hired, not the price agreed. The declared cost is the estimate on the permit application.
DOB NOW General Construction permits begin 2020-12-27; work permitted in the older BIS system before that is invisible, which is why every look-back starts in 2021-08 or later.

Outcomes join on BIN. Joining on BBL as well added about 3 percentage points to the UNSAFE cohort when checked once by hand (81 of 2,543 buildings; not re-derived here) and is left out, so the conversion shares are slightly low rather than high.

The regex definition is narrower than the collector's own PERMIT_RE (no masonry, brick or waterproofing); the work_on_floor definition is narrower still. Both are reported and the claims quote the range.
A share of UNSAFE buildings already had a facade permit in the 180 days before the report (alreadyBefore); they are kept in the denominator, and their later permits are new jobs.

The replays use each filing's own filing_status as of its date, not current_status. The register's enrichment points (ECB, HPD, deeds, sheds, fines) cannot be replayed as they stood on a past date, so the ranking test uses the facade score alone. Cycle-9 auto-generated "No Report Filed" rows carry no date, so the replay cannot tell when one appeared and ignores them; the collector, reading them today, stops calling a building a NON_FILER once one does. Cycle 8 was closed by every replay date, so its auto-generated rows are read as they stand (CHRONIC_NON_FILER).
The unflagged baseline includes buildings that filed this cycle and came back UNSAFE (NOT_FLAGGED_FILED_UNSAFE, 28.9–32.9% within 24 months): the strongest buyers, and no register rule flags them.

Shed removal is the job's sign-off (Letter of Completion); a job never signed off is treated as standing. The shed replay reads shed permits live on the date, aged from the first permit of the live job; a permit's expired_date is the end of its term, not the day the shed came down.

The shed replay is SHED_NO_REPAIR as it should read, not as the collector computes it today: the collector also counts scaffolds, dates a shed from the earliest job the building ever had (so a shed re-erected after a gap looks years old), and treats a wider set of permits (masonry, brick, waterproofing) or a filed job as "repair".
Open windows (openNow) are a snapshot on 2026-09-22: some of those buildings may already have a repair job filed and waiting for its permit (the median job-to-permit time is in facades.jobTiming).
Open data is revised: rerun `npm run backtest` before quoting a figure, and quote it with the dataset loads in `sources`.
